data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes creative thinking performance for 15-year-olds in the Netherlands. The creative thinking test contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating/improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). Results are reported on a 60-point scale, with proficiency levels (e.g., Level 3 baseline and Levels 5–6 top performers) and comparisons to the OECD average and selected countries/economies. The factsheet also reports relationships between creative thinking and mathematics/reading performance (e.g., correlation and the share of variance uniquely explained by mathematics) and documents within-country gaps by socio-economic status and gender. Because this is a descriptive results factsheet rather than an ML study, no predictive model metrics or algorithmic methodology are provided in the excerpt.
